title: Intermittent GPU panics — investigation scrapbook & heuristic checklist
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working scrapbook collecting observed symptoms, lightweight heuristics, quick triage checks, and short-term mitigations for a class of intermittent GPU node kernel panics we've been seeing across multiple racks since mid-2026. Goal: give oncall engineers rapid, ordered checks that historically surfaced the root cause (or temporary mitigation) faster than the generic panic playbook. Not a polished runbook yet — use and iterate.

High-level symptom cluster (common across events):
- Node-level kernel panic with stack trace pointing to nvidia driver context switch or pci error path. Panic happens under steady low-latency inference load (not necessarily peak).
- Correctable ECC spikes preceding panic in 1–10 minute window (soft ECC counts rising).
- NVLink link flapping in dmesg around same time for one or more links (link reset messages and lane CRC errors).
- Some nodes show thermal climb on one GPU followed by peer stalls (one GPU reaches 85–90C but system doesn't trigger hard shutdown).
- Occasional single-process/logs show cuda-context lost and watchdog timeout just prior to panic.

Why this doc exists (lessons so far):
- Generic GPU panic playbook misses correlation between short ECC bursts + NVLink CRCs + non-uniform thermal profiles — that combo often leads to driver state corruption and a kernel panic soon after.
- Quick triage ordering matters: check ECC/NVLink/temperatures before restarting OS; otherwise you may push bad node back into rotation and re-trigger quickly.

Quick heuristic checklist (ordered, ~10–15 minutes to run):
1) Isolate node from load (k8s cordon/drain or Dedicated pool de-schedule). Note: Drain gracefully if possible; prioritise removing serving traffic first.
2) Capture ephemeral logs (do NOT reboot yet):
   - journalctl -k --no-pager --since "-30m" > /tmp/panic-kernel.log
   - dmesg --level=err,alert,crit,emerg > /tmp/dmesg-errs.log
   - nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,UTIL,LINK > /tmp/nvinfo-pre.log
   - collect nvlink stats if driver supports: nvidia-smi nvlink --getstats > /tmp/nvlink-pre.log
3) Check ECC counts: read /var/log/nv_ecc_summary (internal agent) or parse nvidia-smi output. If correctable ECC count has >50x baseline in last 10 minutes and increasing, tag as ECC-burst.
4) Inspect NVLink state: look for CRC mismatch, link reset, lane errors. If nvlink shows repeated lane resets on a particular link/pair, mark link flapping.
5) Thermal profile: run ipmitool sensors or `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,temperature.memory --format=csv` and compare across GPUs on same board. If one GPU >10C above peers, treat as hotspot.
6) PCI/BIOS traces: check /var/log/kern.log for PCIe AER messages, pcieport errors, and root-port resets. If present this points to fabric-layer issues rather than pure DRAM ECC.
7) GPU driver state: look for repeated “GPU reset required” / “GPU has fallen off the bus” messages. If present, don’t re-image OS; escalate to infra kernel-driver team and file a bug with driver logs attached.

If ECC-burst + NVLink-flap present: recommended short-term mitigation before full allocation:
- Keep node cordoned. Power cycle the affected PCIe switch or perform a single-GPU power-cycle (hot-swap script) for the GPU showing highest ECC. Wait for NVLink re-negotiation to settle.
- After power cycle, re-run nvidia-smi nvlink stats and ECC readouts; if counts stop rising and link is stable for 10 minutes under synthetic light load, uncordon with a reduced capacity flag for 24 hours.

If thermal hotspot present:
- Check fan RPMs and BIOS fan curve (ipmitool sdr list). If fan speed reported lower than expected given temp, perform forced fan-profile increase (IPMI command) and mark node for datacenter hardware inspection.

If driver crash / GPU watchdog seen without ECC/NVLink noise:
- Try driver roll-forward to the latest validated build in staging (see linked GH PR). There have been regressions in the 535.x series that show as context switch panics.

Example log excerpts (redacted):
- dmesg snippet (redacted):
  [Aug 30 12:12:13] nvidia: nvlink0: lane CRC error, channel 3 reset
  [Aug 30 12:12:14] device nvme0: AER severity corrected error, PCIe root port reset
  [Aug 30 12:12:16] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=7023, tty=(none), comm="python3"
  [Aug 30 12:12:18] kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: BUG in TX subsystem

- nvidia-smi excerpt: 
  GPU 1 ECC corrected 0->126 in 00:06
  NVLINK: link 1 status: CRC_MISMATCH x5 in last 2m

Known false positives / noise: 
- Minor ECC increments during memory-heavy jobs are normal. Focus on sudden, concentrated bursts across multiple counters.
- Single CRC on NVLink that clears within 30s is likely transient; repeated resets or persistent CRCs are bad.

Investigation notes and hypotheses so far (working):
- Hypothesis A: transient cosmic/soft errors trigger ECC bursts which push PCIe fabric into AER resets and NVLink flapping on susceptible board revisions. Driver's error recovery path sometimes corrupts kernel state if a reset happens during a context switch.
- Hypothesis B: intermittent power rails to GPU VRAM cause sporadic bit flips (manifest as ECC bursts) and lead to NVLink CRCs as memory fetches fail. Thermal hotspots are a contributing factor.
- Hypothesis C: a specific driver + kernel combination has a race in the nvlink error handling path leading to double-free or use-after-free during recovery. May only appear under our inference workload patterns (small, high-frequency kernels).

Data collection plan to validate hypotheses:
- Add short-term tracing to the node: enable tracepoints around nvlink error handlers (ftrace) for nodes in suspected pool (collect for 1–2 days). See GH PR #1298 for instrumentation script.
- On a burnt node, preserve the full /sys/kernel/debug/tracing before reboot. Attach as artifact to JIRA-SRE-4821.
- Run an A/B test: force driver rollback on a candidate node vs keep-driver and exercise with replayed production traces to see error rate delta.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- (Aisha) finish lightweight ftrace wrapper and post to infra repo — due 2026-09-12.
- (Ibrahim) schedule a rack-level hardware sweep for nodes showing ECC bursts >100/day — contact DC on-call and tag for PSU checks — due 2026-09-15.
- (Maya) create a lightweight kube-annotation that marks nodes with recent ECC/NVLink noise to keep them from receiving high-priority jobs for 24h — due 2026-09-09 (in progress).
- (Evan) escalate suspected driver crash pattern to kernel-driver team with collected logs and stack traces, link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1298 — due 2026-09-11.

Runbook draft notes (for later cleanup):
- Include automated pre-drain checks: pull nvinfo, ECC delta, temp delta, nvlink resets in a single script (proto in scripts/gpu-health-check.sh).
- Add an auto-cordon policy when ECC delta > threshold AND nvlink resets seen > 3 in 5m (safe-fail to cordon-only, do not power-cycle automatically).
- Provide a post-mortem template field for these incidents that includes ECC histogram, nvlink reset timeline, thermal timeline, and firmware/driver versions.

Open questions:
- Are we seeing these at higher rates in a specific datacenter/board revision? (DC hardware inventory correlate needed).
- Do Dedicated customers run workloads that correlate more strongly with panics vs hosted? (usage pattern analysis needed).
- What is the acceptable temporary reduced-capacity SLA when we mark nodes as "probation" for 24h? Need Product input.

Quick references / shorthand:
- ECC burst = correctable ECC count increases by >50 over baseline in 10m window.
- NVLINK flap = more than 2 lane resets in 5 minutes on same link pair.
- Hotspot = one GPU >10C above board peers for >2 minutes under steady load.

Appendix: useful commands (copy-pasteable)
- journalctl -k --no-pager --since "-30m" > /tmp/panic-kernel.log
- dmesg --level=err,alert,crit,emerg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-errs.log
- nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,UTIL,LINK -i 0,1,2,3 > /tmp/nvinfo-pre.log
- ipmitool sdr elist | grep -i fan > /tmp/fans.log
- sudo cat /sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl/*/energy_uj (for power anomalies)

Notes to self: keep this free-form until we get consistent repro or driver bug; most value is the ordered checklist that reduces mean-time-to-safe-state. If you add a verified mitigation or precise thresholds, annotate with date and which lab/production experiment validated it.

Recent edits: 2026-09-09 added thermal check and forced-fan mitigation; 2026-09-10 added A/B plan and action owners.

-- end of scrapbook (for now)
